title: RNA binding protein IMP1/ZBP1 drives Actb mRNA localization and local translation in microglial peripheral processes and mediates morphological changes, motility and phagocytosis in response to inflammation
authors: Josune Imaz-Iruretagoyena; Maite Blanco-Urrejola; Irene Núñez-García; Irene García-Toledo; Luis C Fernández-Beltrán; Mar Márquez; Silvia Corrochano; Amanda Sierra; Jimena Baleriola
one_liner_zh: 该文研究RNA结合蛋白IMP1/ZBP1介导Actb mRNA在小胶质细胞突起中的定位与局部翻译，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Polarized cells in the brain, such as neurons and glia, rely on the asymmetric distribution of their proteins compartmentalizing the function of dendrites, axons, glial projections and endfeet. Subcellular proteomes can be assembled either by the transport of proteins synthesized in the cell soma or by the delivery of mRNAs to target compartments where they are locally translated into protein. This latter mechanism is known as local protein synthesis or local translation, and it has been best studied in neurons. Increasing evidence suggest it is also required to maintain local protein homeostasis in glial cells, however, in microglia, local translation remains largely unexplored. Given the scant evidence, we aimed at exploring the existence of local translation in peripheral microglial processes (PeMPs) and unravel its functional significance in response to inflammation, a major hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases. We report that local translation in PeMPs is enhanced by triggering a microglial inflammatory response with bacterial lipopolysaccharides (LPS). We found that Actb mRNA polarizes to PeMPs and is locally translated upon LPS exposure. mRNA localization in eukaryotic cells is driven by RNA binding proteins. Interestingly, downregulation of the Actb binding protein IMP1/ZBP1 impaired Actb mRNA polarization and its localized translation, and led to defects in filopodia distribution, PeMP motility, lamellar directed migration and phagocytosis in microglia. Thus, our work contributes to recent findings that mRNA localization and localized translation occur in microglia and gives a mechanistic insight into the relevance of this molecular mechanism in fundamental microglial functions in response to inflammation.
abstract_zh: 大脑中的极化细胞，如神经元和胶质细胞，依赖于其蛋白质的不对称分布，以区隔树突、轴突、胶质突起和终足的功能。亚细胞蛋白质组可以通过细胞体合成的蛋白质运输来组装，也可以通过将mRNA递送至靶区室并在局部翻译成蛋白质来组装。后一种机制被称为局部蛋白质合成或局部翻译，并在神经元中研究最为深入。越来越多的证据表明，这一机制对于维持胶质细胞中的局部蛋白质稳态也是必需的，然而，在小胶质细胞中，局部翻译在很大程度上仍未得到探索。鉴于证据稀少，我们旨在探索外周小胶质突起（PeMPs）中局部翻译的存在，并揭示其在炎症反应中的功能意义，而炎症是神经退行性疾病的一个主要标志。我们报告，通过用细菌脂多糖（LPS）触发小胶质细胞炎症反应，PeMPs中的局部翻译得到增强。我们发现，Actb mRNA在LPS暴露下极化至PeMPs并被局部翻译。真核细胞中的mRNA定位由RNA结合蛋白驱动。有趣的是，下调Actb结合蛋白IMP1/ZBP1损害了Actb mRNA的极化及其局部翻译，并导致小胶质细胞中丝状伪足分布、PeMP运动性、片状定向迁移和吞噬作用的缺陷。因此，我们的工作为近期关于mRNA定位和局部翻译在小胶质细胞中发生的发现做出了贡献，并为这一分子机制在小胶质细胞对炎症反应的基本功能中的相关性提供了机制性见解。
